summary: APAC traffic intermittently routed through EU egress proxy causing queued inference requests and timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
- Starting 2026-03-10 08:20 UTC, customers in APAC (notably Aurora Maps) reported elevated P95/P99 token latency and intermittent 504s for generation requests.
Impact:
- Approximately 12% of requests from ap-southeast-1 to Redwood hosted API experienced >500ms additional TTFB and occasional 504s during the 08:20–09:40 UTC window. Customer-visible: slow map annotation generation and occasional failed jobs.
Environment:
- Production, hosted API fronted by API gateway, smart-routing enabled, default routing policy: prefer local region then fallback. Dedicated customer pool in ap-southeast-1.
Steps to reproduce:
1) From an APAC client with region hint ap-southeast-1, issue text generation requests pinned to redwood-2.3-8k.
2) Observe p50/p95/p99 from our ingestion logs and customer request IDs during spike window.
Observed behavior:
- Traceroutes from gateway to serving nodes show an unexpected egress hop to eu-west-1 proxy cluster before reaching serving runtime.
- Streaming sessions sometimes stall for >2s during handshake, causing client-side timeouts.
Expected behavior:
- Traffic for ap-southeast-1 should egress locally to nearby serving pools, with fallback to other APAC capacity, not EU.
Logs / evidence:
- Sample request IDs: req_AK92-xx, req_BM34-yy, req_CZ11-zz (all show proxy hop to 18.197.x.y eu-west egress cluster).
- Dashboard: p95 increased from 180ms -> 740ms; p99 from 650ms -> 2.3s.
- Envoy metrics show a cluster weight change for egress-proxy-apac -> egress-proxy-eu had been applied at 08:15 UTC by config sync job.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
- 08:14 UTC: config-sync job (cfg-sync-3) deployed a routing delta intended for a canary in EU; the change included a malformed selector that matched 'egress-proxy.apac' service name.
- 08:15 UTC: automated deployment propagated the selector to global envoy control plane; APAC edge nodes started resolving to EU egress cluster.
- 08:20–09:40 UTC: increased queue lengths on eu-west egress proxies and increased RTT for APAC sessions.
- Network traces (tcpdump) show added RTT of ~180–300ms per request due to cross-region hop.
Hypothesis:
- A configuration selector typo (regex vs. exact match) in routing delta caused accidental global promotion of EU egress cluster for APAC endpoints.
- The smart-routing fallback logic treated the EU cluster as same-priority rather than fallback, leading to sticky routing while EU cluster experienced load.
Evidence collected:
- cfg-sync job logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/5221 (line 413–421) shows selector ".*egress-proxy.*" used instead of exact "egress-proxy-eu".
- Envoy cluster assignment changed: archived snapshots at 08:16 show apac edges resolving to eu cluster IPs.
- No hardware failures; GPU pools healthy in ap-southeast-1 during window.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:55 UTC - Sofia Martinez (Support): Initial triage with customer. Customer reported p99s of ~2s and occasional 504s. Collected request IDs and asked for timeframe. Escalated to SRE.
2026-03-10 09:10 UTC - Daniel Chen (SRE): Observed unusual cluster assignments in control plane. Initiated delta rollback of cfg-sync-3 to restore previous selectors. Placing ticket as P1.

2026-03-10 09:22 UTC - Daniel Chen (SRE): Rolled back the config at 09:20 UTC. APAC edges mark eu cluster assignments cleared by 09:25 UTC. Early telemetry shows p95 returning toward baseline. Notifying customer and monitoring.
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Aurora Maps (Customer): Confirmed reduced failures; p95 approximating normal but asked for root cause and fix plan to prevent recurrence.

2026-03-11 15:30 UTC - Network Eng (Priyanka Rao): Added patch to cfg-sync to enforce exact-match selectors and added unit tests to prevent wildcard promotion. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-config/pull/211

2026-03-12 11:00 UTC - Daniel Chen (SRE): Deployed patch to staging and promoted after 6h of green. Added additional monitoring alarms on Envoy cluster weight drift and an automated rollback if an env group's cluster weight shifts >15% unexpectedly.
resolution:
Immediate workaround: Rolled back cfg-sync-3 at 09:20 UTC which restored correct egress cluster assignment for APAC edges and reduced cross-region routing.
Permanent fix: Updated cfg-sync pipeline to validate selectors as exact-match; added CI unit tests and a production safety gate to block deploys that would change egress cluster weights by >10% without manual approval.
Follow-ups:
- PR merged: routing-config #211.
- Runbook updated: egress-routing-runbook (confluence).
- Post-incident: SRE to perform audit of past 30 days of cfg-sync deltas for similar selector patterns.
Customer communication: Shared timeline and mitigations with Aurora Maps; offered 1 month of credit for impacted usage and scheduled a follow-up technical review on 2026-03-17.
